title: ledger_lock's holder judges its own lock by inode number alone, so after a stale clear a reused inode lets it remove the next writer's live lock
goal: SP-6jfnx5i3 review G3 (BG-s3iuw4x2): the holder removes the lock on exit when lock.stat().st_ino equals the inode it made (_tools/bl_base.py ledger_lock), and ext4 and tmpfs hand a freed inode number to the next file at once, so a holder slower than the stale age whose lock a waiter cleared can unlink the next writer's lock and let a third process in beside it; the stale clearer already compares (st_ino, st_mtime_ns). The holder removes the lock only when both the inode and the modification time it recorded at create still match.

run:
import os,sys,tempfile,types,pathlib as P;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_base as b
d=P.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());led=d/'c.json';lock=d/'c.json.lock'
rf=os.fstat;os.fstat=lambda fd:types.SimpleNamespace(st_ino=4242,st_mtime_ns=1,st_mtime=0)
rs=P.Path.stat
with b.ledger_lock(led):
    os.fstat=rf
    lock.unlink();lock.write_text('')
    P.Path.stat=lambda self,*a,**k:(types.SimpleNamespace(st_ino=4242,st_mtime_ns=2,st_mtime=rs(self).st_mtime) if self==lock else rs(self,*a,**k))
P.Path.stat=rs;kept=lock.exists()
print('the next writer lock kept when the first holder exits after an inode reuse:',kept);sys.exit(0 if kept else 1)

repro_reason: APFS does not reuse inode numbers at once, so the reuse is planted by patching os.fstat and Path.stat; the run drives ledger_lock itself
